mmap.interpretation: MMap is a multi-resolution map image family; the selected frame is later clipped/scaled into the 128×128 destination rather than being a 128×128 source itself.

fmmap.common_offsets: Frames 0–28 generally carry WIL offsetX=-24, offsetY=-16; Frame 30 is offsetX=0, offsetY=0.
fmmap.interpretation: FMMap is the full-map/large-map resource family; the original server cross-reference maps overland/city entries to its frames. Its dimensions are materially larger than the fixed minimap destination and must be displayed through a scroll/zoom viewport.

static_initializer_trace.interpretation: The executable initializes both map libraries and a 128×128 surface before any map ID is selected. This is stronger than inferring the map source from a screenshot: the two library fields and the branch-specific frame-header path are statically explicit.

viewport.surface_size_basis: The constructor at 0x0043D4D0 calls 0x0043D5F0 with width=128 and height=128; 0x0043DE40 later rebuilds the same surface as 256×256 or 128×128.

fixed_minimap_widget.basis: The initializer pushes bottom=0x80, right=0x320, top=0 and left=0x2A0 before the SetRect IAT call for owner+0x2C0.
fixed_minimap_widget.interpretation: This is the original fixed 800x600 minimap destination at the top-right edge. The constructor passes a 128×128 map surface; the display-mode routine can rebuild it as 256×256.

viewport.notes: The map subsystem maintains a source/view rectangle and selects a 4096 or 6144 surface mode based on loaded map metadata. The destination widget rectangle is now statically recovered as 128x128 at screen (672,0).

closed_notes.closed: Map -> library/frame binding for simulator fully wired: client primary-static select rule 0x0043D780 (map_id >= 1000 -> FMMap.wil frame map_id-1000, else MMap.wil frame map_id) + server MiniMap.txt crossref (minimap-server-crossref.json, 182 crossref-confirmed rows) -> map_bindings.json emitted by build_mir3_simulator_data.py; simulator map switching (setCurrentMap) updates BOTH map.bg and map.minimap from the same binding record. Evidence level: derived (client rule primary-static + server binding secondary).

Type 0x32 map-object business name = server-supplied blocking minimap marker (candidate: teleport/block marker; NOT an NPC). Evidence chain: map-object list head 0x560070 / tail 0x56008C / count 0x560098, doubly-linked nodes {vtable 0x476448, +4=object ptr, +8=prev, +0xC=next}; node object +0x88=type byte (dword, low byte), +0xCC/+0xD0=world X/Y. List is populated ONLY by network spawn/update handlers (~0x407Fxx parses pkt+0xB type byte -> obj+0x61BD4, name at pkt+0xC -> obj+8, sprite via 0x4014F0 -> obj+0x61C70, X/Y words at pkt+6/8; find-by-id 0x4350B9; child list 0x560088). Exhaustive scan of ALL byte-store (24 encodings '88 /r,88') and dword-store (27 hits, all unrelated structs) encodings against +0x88 found ZERO writes of value 0x32 -> type byte arrives only from server packets. Paint 0x43DA80 @0x43DC54-0x43DCB8: cmp byte [edi+0x88],0x32 -> draws small yellow (0xFFFF) marker rect at (obj+0xCC, obj+0xD0) at 1.5 px/world-unit. Blocking: 0x4123E3 returns movement-blocked when the object at [0x7E335C] (targeted-object global) has type byte 0x32, plus PtInRect(0x724FFC) gate @0x412397. Targeting/use excluded: position finder 0x41ECAE returns only types 0/1 (0x32 excluded); type dispatch sites 0x408276/0x40DFF0/0x411955/0x43CD29 handle 0/1/3 (kind words 0x1A/0x71/0x72/0x73 at +0x8A, name at +8) - never 0x32. Server MiniMap.txt is map-name->frame-index only (no type semantics). Residual gap: exact business name (teleport vs generic block point) requires a server packet trace or runtime frame capture; candidate stands as teleport/block marker.

Minimap user-facing label EXISTS: '小地图(Ctrl+V, V)' GBK string at 0x47BCCC (rdata block 0x47BBCC-0x47BCF4 = 17 'label(key)' hotkey-guide pairs), bound as a button label at screen+0x5730 via 0x417550 caller 0x4279CF (button IDs 0x52/0x53, pos (viewX+0xE4, viewY+2); screen object = main+0x2A548C, buttons stride 0xB4 to 0x61BC). The 0x54 zoom toggle ('T') has NO user-facing label: exhaustive GBK scans (放大/缩小/缩放/放大镜/帮助/热键 + T-related) = 0 hits; only 2 地图 hits total (0x47B568 '此处没有可以显示的地图' in the map-change no-map path @0x420C50, and the label block) and 1 小地图 hit (0x47BCCC). Keyboard dispatch 0x42CE90 (GetAsyncKeyState via IAT 0x476278, chain 0x42CC76-0x42CF1F): VK 0x54='T', gated on [screen+0x6518]==1 (map open), toggles [screen+0x64A8] -> 0x43D5F0(screen+0x6214, 0x100,0x100) @0x42CED2 / (0x80,0x80) @0x42CEF0. V (0x56) @0x42CDDA opens/closes the map panel (0x451770 on 0x8AB828, 0x64 ms debounce); mouse path 0x42C270 (3 s debounce) also toggles; menu path 0x422BC5 (flag [esi+0x2AB9A4]). No mouse-wheel zoom: exhaustive WM_MOUSEWHEEL (0x20A) scan (all 8 compare encodings) = 0 hits; mouse over minimap = hit-test 0x43DDB0 (caller 0x42BDC0) + Ctrl+drag reposition 0x43DEB0 (caller 0x42C75C). 0x43DE40 has ZERO callers and zero imm32/vtable refs -> dead/legacy code (live zoom inlined in T-key handler). Map window object identity reconciled: member screen+0x6214 == main+0x2AB6A0 (screen object = main+0x2A548C), since map-change handler 0x420C3C calls 0x43D780 with this=main+0x2AB6A0 and the keyboard dispatch/update driver use this=screen+0x6214. Mode 256x256 vs 128x128 = LARGER VIEWPORT (coverage), NOT zoom-out rendering the same 128x128 widget at higher source resolution. 0x43D5F0 full static: stores view W/H unclamped at +0x2B8/+0x2BC; SetRect(&+0x2C0, 800-min(w,frameW), 0, 800, min(h,frameH)) via IAT 0x4762B0 (frame dims from [0x2E0..0x2E8]/[0x2E4..0x2EC], set by map-select 0x43D780); releases old surface +0x00 and creates a new surface at w x h -> 256 mode = 256x256 widget at (544,0,800,256), 128 mode = 128x128 widget at (672,0,800,128); surface size ALWAYS == widget size, blitted 1:1 at the same 1.5 px/world-unit scale ([0x476904] factor) -> 256 mode shows 4x the map area. Scroll semantics: source/scroll rect at +0x2D0 derived from world pos (SetRect x,y,x+[2B8],y+[2BC]; centering via cdq/sar; clamps to [0, frameW-viewW]/[0, frameH-viewH]; ftol 0x468520); WIL frame decoded 1:1 (0x465560: dest col = x-x0, row = row-y0) -> offset-with-scroll, no scale-to-fit. Per-frame driver 0x4295AC (when [screen+0x6518]!=0): 0x43D850(screen+0x6214, playerX from [0x777764], playerY from [0x777768]) then paint 0x43DA80. 0x43D5F0 external callers = only T-key 0x42CED2/0x42CEF0 (internal 0x43D5DE/0x43D7E3/0x43D831/0x43DE73/0x43DE96). Residual gap (optional): runtime frame capture to visually confirm no scaling; the static chain is complete.
